page_metadata.title: Adapting existing toxicokinetic models to relate perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl intake to biomarkers in humans

stated_assumptions.description: Saturable reabsorption from the filtrate compartment to the central compartment via Michaelis–Menten kinetics.
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: a saturable process with a Michaelis–Menten kinetics dictates reabsorption from the filtrate compartment to the central compartment

stated_assumptions.description: Bioavailability parameter added to align with the model implemented by the EPA for PFOS and PFOA.
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: a parameter for bioavailability was added to the model to align with the model implemented by the , in their final reference dose level setting for PFOS and PFOA

stated_assumptions.description: Bioavailability initially set at 90% for both compounds to reflect a high fraction of an administered dose reaching systemic circulation after oral ingestion.
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: The bioavailability was initially set at 90% for both compounds to reflect a high fraction of an administered dose reaching systemic circulation after oral ingestion

stated_assumptions.description: The model does not include a development compartment, thus underestimating serum levels in children and young adults by excluding gestation and breastfeeding exposures.
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: Data for individuals <20 years of age were excluded from the fitting process because the TK model does not include a development compartment and thus underestimates serum levels in children and young adults by excluding gestation and breastfeeding exposures

stated_assumptions.description: The saturable resorption process is assumed to be minimal for PFBS due to its short half-life (<7 days).
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: we decided not to pursue the study of this compound further

stated_assumptions.description: The proportion of free compound in serum (Free), absorption rate (ka), and inter-compartmental rates (k12, k21) were assigned set values from iterative evaluation of starting parameters.
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: the proportion of free compound in the serum ( Free ), the rate of absorption from the gut ( k a ), and the rate to and from the second compartment ( k 12 , k 21 ) were assigned set values from the iterative evaluation of the starting parameters
stated_assumptions.source_location: Model parameters estimated for humans for both PFOA and PFOS

stated_assumptions.description: The animal models were scaled to humans by adjusting cardiac blood output (QCC) to 12.5 L/h/kg^0.74.
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: We scaled the reparametrized Wambaugh model from Part I to humans using human values for the bodyweight (70 kg) and cardiac output (12.5 L/h/kg 0.74 ) following the procedure of ; We then adjusted the maximum rate of the saturable resorption parameter ( T m , mg/h) to match the half-life estimated in humans from an exposure study deemed to be representative of the general population
stated_assumptions.source_location: TK modeling approach: a case study with PFOS and PFOA

stated_assumptions.description: The saturable resorption rate (Tmc) was fitted for a half-life of 3.4 years and 2.7 years for PFOS and PFOA, respectively.
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: The animal models were scaled to humans by adjusting the cardiac blood output ( QCC ) to 12.5 L/h/kg 0.74 and fitting a saturable resorption rate ( Tmc ) for a half-life of 3.4 years and 2.7 years for PFOS and PFOA, respectively
stated_assumptions.source_location: Model parameters estimated for humans for both PFOA and PFOS

stated_assumptions.description: The PFOA bioAv and Kt parameters were refit to the nonhuman primate data assuming a bioavailability of 90% for application in the human model.
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: the PFOA bioAv and K t parameters, which were refit to the nonhuman primate data assuming a bioavailability of 90% for application in the human model, as the lower bioavailability observed in the nonhuman primate model was assumed to be the result of experiment-specific conditions
stated_assumptions.source_location: Model parameters estimated for humans for both PFOA and PFOS

stated_assumptions.description: The human model is associated with a clearance of approximately 0.06 mL/kg-day for a 70 kg adult for doses well below saturation (<1000 mg/kg BW/day).
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: Notably, for doses well below saturation (<1000 mg/kg BW/day), the human model is associated with a clearance of approximately 0.06 mL/kg-day for a 70 kg adult

dosing.source_quote: The PFOS model predicted serum levels with an MSLE of 0.07 (Fig. 3) and an underlying exposure model that peaked in 1990 at 14.9 ng PFOS/kg BW/day, fell to 2.5 ng PFOS/kg BW/day in 1998, and continued decreasing to 0.24 ng PFOS/kg BW/day in 2017 (Fig. S5).

The PFOA model more closely predicted the NHANES observed serum levels with an MSLE of 0.03 (Fig. 4) and an underlying exposure model that increased from 0.45 ng/kg BW/day in 1990 to 1.1 ng/kg BW/day in 1998 and fell to 0.13 ng/kg BW/day in 2017 (Fig. S6).

The PFOS model predicted serum levels with an MSLE of 0.07 (Fig. 3) and an underlying exposure model that peaked in 1990 at 14.9 ng PFOS/kg BW/day, fell to 2.5 ng PFOS/kg BW/day in 1998, and continued decreasing to 0.24 ng PFOS/kg BW/day in 2017 (Fig. S5).

The PFOA model more closely predicted the NHANES observed serum levels with an MSLE of 0.03 (Fig. 4) and an underlying exposure model that increased from 0.45 ng/kg BW/day in 1990 to 1.1 ng/kg BW/day in 1998 and fell to 0.13 ng/kg BW/day in 2017 (Fig. S6).

author_stated_limitations: The model does not include a development compartment, thus underestimating serum levels in children and young adults by excluding gestation and breastfeeding exposures.
we decided not to pursue the study of this compound further
The saturable resorption process is assumed to be minimal for PFBS due to its short half-life (<7 days).
evaluator_judgments.data_independence_assessment: The model parameters were fitted using nonhuman primate data and scaled to humans, and the model was applied to PFHxS without additional calibration data. The model was not explicitly validated against independent human data beyond the exposure scenarios used for fitting, so data independence cannot be confirmed.
